concerns: The bare cue “gear shift” can refer to either the control or the selected gear, but this is resolved by narrowing it.
response.cue_rationale: Both answers refer to the control used to select a vehicle gear; the rewrite avoids ambiguity with the gear/result itself.

preference_risk.rationale: More explicit Malaysian forms such as “gear lever” or “tuil gear” may occur alongside the shorter everyday form “gear.”

response.rationale: “Persneling” is the ordinary Indonesian term for the vehicle gear-shift control, while Malaysian Malay commonly uses “gear” in this context. The pair teaches a useful everyday national preference.
response.risk_rationale: Malaysian usage varies between the shorter “gear” and more explicit forms such as “gear lever” or “tuil gear.”
response.shared_synonym_rationale: “Gear lever” or “tuil gear” may also occur in Malaysian Malay, but “gear” remains a credible everyday preference in the proposed pairing.
